01-information-and-distinguishability: Information is physical, and a physical carrier encodes messages only to the extent that different preparations produce statistically distinguishable measurement outcomes.
Perfect single-shot distinguishability requires mutually exclusive outcome supports; overlapping probability distributions inevitably introduce identification error.
Operational tasks—compression, noisy transmission, state discrimination, and privacy—define the quantitative measures of both classical and quantum information theory.
02-classical-information: Shannon entropy \(H(X) = -\sum_x p(x)\log_2 p(x)\) measures the expected surprise of a source and sets the asymptotic limit of lossless data compression at \(H(X)\) bits per symbol.
Joint entropy, conditional entropy \(H(X|Y)\), and mutual information \(I(X:Y) = H(X) - H(X|Y)\) quantify how much observing one random variable reduces uncertainty about another.
Shannon’s noisy-channel coding theorem establishes that reliable communication over a discrete memoryless channel is possible up to capacity \(C = \max_{p(x)} I(X:Y)\).
03-quantum-states: Pure quantum states are unit vectors \(|\psi\rangle\) in a complex Hilbert space up to global phase, where coherent superpositions exhibit interference that classical probability mixtures cannot reproduce.
Projective measurements in an orthonormal basis \(\{|b_k\rangle\}\) yield outcome \(k\) with Born probability \(p(k) = |\langle b_k|\psi\rangle|^2\) and project the system onto \(|b_k\rangle\).
Unitary operators \(U^\dagger U = I\) preserve inner products \(\langle\phi|\psi\rangle\), so no unitary transformation can change the overlap or distinguishability of two states.
04-composite-systems: The joint Hilbert space of composite systems \(A\) and \(B\) is the tensor product \(\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B\), whose dimension grows multiplicatively as \(d_A d_B\).

Product states \(|\psi\rangle_A \otimes |\phi\rangle_B\) exhibit independent local statistics, whereas entangled states such as the Bell basis cannot be factored into separate subsystem state vectors.

Every bipartite pure state admits a Schmidt decomposition \(|\Psi\rangle_{AB} = \sum_i \sqrt{\lambda_i}|u_i\rangle_A|v_i\rangle_B\), whose positive Schmidt coefficients \(\lambda_i\) completely characterize its bipartite entanglement.
05-mixed-states: A density operator \(\rho = \sum_j p_j |\psi_j\rangle\langle\psi_j|\) is a positive semidefinite operator of trace one that captures both classical ensemble uncertainty and entanglement with unobserved subsystems.

Every expectation value and measurement probability depends only on \(\rho\) via \(\langle M\rangle = \mathrm{Tr}(\rho M)\), so distinct ensembles with the same density matrix are operationally indistinguishable.
The partial trace \(\rho_A = \mathrm{Tr}_B(\rho_{AB})\) is the unique operation that reproduces all local measurement statistics on subsystem \(A\) alone.
06-quantum-operations: Physical transformations of open quantum systems are completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) linear maps—quantum channels \(\mathcal{E}(\rho)\).

By the Kraus and Stinespring theorems, every quantum channel can be written both as an operator sum \(\mathcal{E}(\rho) = \sum_k K_k \rho K_k^\dagger\) with \(\sum_k K_k^\dagger K_k = I\) and as unitary coupling to an environment followed by partial trace.
Canonical qubit noise models—depolarizing, phase damping, and amplitude damping—contract the Bloch ball in characteristic ways and obey the data-processing inequality.
07-quantum-measurement: The most general measurement statistics are described by a positive operator-valued measure (POVM) \(\{E_m\}\) with \(E_m \ge 0\) and \(\sum_m E_m = I\), where \(p(m) = \mathrm{Tr}(E_m\rho)\).
Naimark’s dilation theorem guarantees that any POVM on system \(A\) can be realized by coupling an ancilla \(B\) unitarily and performing an ordinary projective measurement on \(AB\).

When post-measurement states matter, measurement operators \(M_m\) satisfying \(E_m = M_m^\dagger M_m\) update the state via \(\rho_m = M_m\rho M_m^\dagger / \mathrm{Tr}(E_m\rho)\), trading information gain against state disturbance.
08-state-discrimination: Non-orthogonal quantum states \(\langle\psi_0|\psi_1\rangle \neq 0\) cannot be distinguished with zero error in a single copy.

Minimum-error discrimination between two states is solved by the Helstrom bound \(p_{\mathrm{succ}} = \frac{1}{2}\bigl(1 + \|p_0\rho_0 - p_1\rho_1\|_1\bigr)\), achieved by projecting onto the positive and negative eigenspaces of \(p_0\rho_0 - p_1\rho_1\).

Unambiguous state discrimination uses a three-outcome POVM to eliminate false identifications completely at the price of an inconclusive outcome occurring with probability at least \(|\langle\psi_0|\psi_1\rangle|\).
09-information-constraints: The no-cloning and no-broadcasting theorems forbid any unitary or channel from copying an arbitrary unknown state \(|\psi\rangle \mapsto |\psi\rangle\otimes|\psi\rangle\) because linearity and inner-product preservation conflict for non-orthogonal states.
The no-signaling theorem ensures that local measurements or channels applied on Bob’s share of an entangled state never alter Alice’s reduced density matrix \(\rho_A\).
Monogamy of entanglement limits how strongly a single quantum system can be entangled with two different partners simultaneously.
10-entanglement-protocols: Quantum teleportation consumes one shared ebit \(|\Phi^+\rangle_{AB}\) and two classical bits from Alice’s Bell measurement to transfer an unknown qubit state \(|\psi\rangle\) to Bob without sending a physical qubit across the channel.
Superdense coding reverses the resource trade-off: applying one of four local Pauli gates to half of a shared Bell pair lets a single transmitted qubit convey two bits of classical information.
Entanglement swapping applies a joint Bell measurement on two independent entangled pairs \(AB\) and \(CD\) to entangle remote terminals \(A\) and \(D\) that have never interacted directly.
11-quantum-entropy: The von Neumann entropy \(S(\rho) = -\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\log_2\rho) = -\sum_i \lambda_i\log_2\lambda_i\) equals zero for pure states and reaches \(\log_2 d\) for the maximally mixed state \(I/d\).

Unlike classical conditional entropy, quantum conditional entropy \(S(A|B) = S(AB) - S(B)\) can be negative when \(AB\) is entangled, while quantum mutual information \(I(A:B) = S(A)+S(B)-S(AB)\) can reaches \(2\log_2 d\).
Strong subadditivity \(S(ABC) + S(B) \le S(AB) + S(BC)\) and monotonicity of relative entropy \(D(\rho\|\sigma)\) under quantum channels anchor all fundamental quantum coding bounds.
12-quantum-compression: Schumacher’s noiseless coding theorem proves that an i.i.d. quantum source emitting ensemble state \(\rho\) can be compressed to \(S(\rho)\) qubits per source symbol with asymptotically vanishing infidelity.
Compression works by projecting \(\rho^{\otimes n}\) onto its typical subspace of dimension \(\approx 2^{nS(\rho)}\), which captures nearly all probability weight as \(n \to \infty\).
Attempting to compress below \(S(\rho)\) qubits per symbol forces the entanglement fidelity with a purifying reference system to decay toward zero.
13-entanglement-transformations: Under local operations and classical communication (LOCC), entanglement is a resource that can never increase on average.

Nielsen’s theorem shows that a pure bipartite state \(|\psi\rangle\) transforms deterministically into \(|\phi\rangle\) by LOCC if and only if the Schmidt vector of \(|\psi\rangle\) is majorized by that of \(|\phi\rangle\).

Asymptotically, pure states convert reversibly at the entanglement-entropy rate \(S(\rho_A)\), whereas mixed states exhibit an irreversibility gap between entanglement cost \(E_C\) and distillable entanglement \(E_D\), including bound entanglement.
14-quantum-error-correction: Quantum error correction protects unknown superpositions by encoding \(k\) logical qubits into an entangled \(n\)-qubit subspace so local errors map the code space into mutually orthogonal syndrome subspaces.
Measuring stabilizer generators extracts a discrete classical error syndrome without collapsing the encoded logical superposition \(\alpha|0_L\rangle + \beta|1_L\rangle\).
By the Knill–Laflamme conditions \(P E_a^\dagger E_b P = c_{ab} P\), discretizing continuous Pauli errors into \(I, X, Z, Y\) suffices to correct arbitrary single-qubit channels.
15-quantum-communication: The Holevo bound \(\chi = S(\sum_x p_x\rho_x) - \sum_x p_x S(\rho_x)\) caps the accessible classical mutual information extractable from an ensemble, and the Holevo–Schumacher–Westmoreland (HSW) theorem achieves this rate using collective measurements.
Entanglement-assisted classical capacity simplifies additively to a single-letter quantum mutual information formula.

The quantum capacity \(Q(\mathcal{N})\) for transmitting intact qubits and entanglement is governed by the regularized coherent information \(I_c(\rho, \mathcal{N}) = S(\mathcal{N}(\rho)) - S((\mathcal{N}\otimes I)(|\Psi_ho\rangle))\).
16-quantum-cryptography: Quantum key distribution protocols such as BB84 and E91 leverage non-orthogonal states or entanglement monogamy so any eavesdropping attempt by Eve introduces detectable disturbance in parameter estimation.
Converting raw sifted detections into a secure key requires classical information reconciliation (error correction) followed by privacy amplification using universal hash functions.
Finite-key composable security bounds the trace distance between the final shared key and an ideal uniform key that is completely decoupled from Eve’s quantum side information \(E\).
